cover.title: Fast and slow
cover.lead: Two pointers walk a list, one step and two steps at a time. Where they meet, or where fast runs out, tells you something.
cover.use_it_when: You need a list's middle, or must know if it loops, with no extra memory.
cover.why_it_matters: One idea answers two classic questions in O(1) space: the middle node and the loop.
cover.promise: You'll find a loop in {lines} lines.

final.caption: They meet after {{ROUNDS}} rounds: the list loops.

slides.title: Two runners
slides.scene: Two friends run, one twice as fast. On a straight road the fast one just reaches the end. On a round track, the fast one comes up behind the slow one.

blocks.text: Inside a loop, fast gains [[one node]] per round, so it can't jump over slow.

slides.title: Round by round
slides.lead: Gold is slow, steel is fast. In the loop 3 4 5 6, the gap shrinks by one each round.

quickcheck.question: Same nodes 1 to 6, but no loop. Where is slow when fast runs out?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: node {{MIDDLE}}. Fast went twice as far, so slow is halfway.

lines: while fast != none and fast.next != none:

blocks.text: Of the two middles, 3 and 4, this returns the second.

slides.title: Find a loop

lines: while fast != none and fast.next != none:

slides.explain: Line 14 compares the nodes, not their values. If fast falls off the end, line 16 says there is no loop.

slides.teaser: The check that stops a crash
slides.title: Check fast first
slides.lead: Check only fast.next on line 11. With an even list, fast lands on none, and none has no next.

cost.note: In a loop, fast gains one node a round, so they meet within one lap.

blog.summary: Move one pointer 1 step and another 2 steps: if they meet, the list loops; when the fast one runs out, the slow one is in the middle.
blog.tested_what: The loop check and the middle node
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked lists (1 to 6 with and without a loop, odd and even lengths, the LeetCode 141 examples, one node with and without a loop to itself, an empty list, 10,000 nodes looping to the start, the end and nowhere) and random lists of up to 12 nodes, half of them with a loop
blog.tested_against: the loop position the test built the list with, and the middle index of the list
blog.tested_extra: The rounds in the walk-through, the quick-check answer and the trap's crash come from running the code.

caption.first: Fast and slow pointers explained: detect a loop in a linked list (LeetCode 141) and find its middle node (LeetCode 876) in O(1) space.
lines: Slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2. In a loop, fast gains one node a round and meets slow.
No loop: when fast runs out, slow is in the middle.
The trap: check only fast.next and an even-length list crashes when fast becomes none.
